Do you want to help build some of the largest and most consequential enterprise and customer technology systems in the world? Join Apple’s Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization. IS&T is the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. It’s Apple’s central nervous system. Supporting 2.5 billion active Apple devices, processing billions of secure transactions, and keeping the technology that defines modern life running flawlessly, IS&T makes the impossible feel effortless.Do you love building solutions to handle global complexity and immense scale? Imagine what you could do here.
At Apple, new ideas have a way of becoming extraordinary products, services, and customer experiences. Bring passion and dedication to your job and there's no telling what you could accomplish. That same passion for innovation that goes into our products also applies to our practices, strengthening our dedication to leave the world better than we found it!
Most software engineering roles hand off testing to one team and operations to another. Here you own all of it. As a Software Engineer on Forge, you'll design, build, test, ship, and run the platform Apple's engineering teams build on, working closely with those teams to find where the infrastructure beneath them gets in the way and fixing it.
Forge is part of Enterprise Technology Services (ETS), within Apple's Information Systems and Technology (IS&T) organization, the engine behind everything Apple does for customers and for the people who build for them. Forge is building the platform Apple's engineering organizations can use to take a service from code to running in production. That path has traditionally run through a series of separate specialist systems. We are bringing it together on a common platform with a shared core, so a team goes from allocated capacity to a live production service without assembling the pieces themselves. Our job is to get teams to production quickly, on a platform that stays secure and reliable without them having to think about it.
Our charter is deliberately wide and still growing, reaching from the physical fleet in the data center to the surfaces engineering teams build against, and extending into new environments and new classes of infrastructure as Apple's needs evolve. We are a small team with outsized reach, bringing an AI-first mindset to how the platform operates and improves itself, and the best work we do takes one team's hardest problem and turns it into a capability every team inherits.
You will work with product owners, infrastructure owners, and partner engineers to turn ambiguous, high-impact problems into clean solutions. You'll own products that ETS teams depend on every day. You will also help define how AI agents work in production alongside humans, in the same codebases our engineers ship to daily.
The role mixes product engineering with hands-on integration work. You may start closer to one than the other, and you should be comfortable moving between them as the work changes.
We are looking for strong full-stack engineers who have owned work through production, have built something with LLMs or agents, can design securely and for scale, and want to grow into leading designs and mentoring others.
Own features and integrations from design to production for an enterprise web application: data model, services, APIs, and an accessible UI
Design and build agentic workflows that take part in real operational processes, with approvals, guardrails, and audit trails built in
Make our data AI-ready by exposing it through well-defined interfaces that agents can query and act on reliably
Build and maintain integrations with internal systems, and the automation that helps teams adopt common standards
Design for security and scale: threat modeling, authentication and authorization, least privilege, and designs that fail gracefully
Operate what you ship: define SLIs and SLOs, instrument with metrics, logs, and traces, build dashboards and alerts, and join on-call
Partner with product owners, infrastructure teams, and engineering peers to scope problems and prototype solutions quickly
Present your designs in design reviews, take part in reviewing others' work, and help teammates grow through code reviews and pairing
Minimum Qualifications
B.S. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
5+ years of professional software development, with a track record of owning features or integrations through production
Full-stack experience: a backend language such as Java (Spring Boot or similar) and a modern web UI framework such as React or Angular
Experience designing features with security principles (threat modeling, authentication and authorization, least privilege, secure data handling) and scalable patterns (stateless services, caching, asynchronous messaging, retries, circuit breakers, back-pressure), and explaining your trade-offs in design reviews
Have built an LLM- or agent-based feature, whether in production, as a prototype, or as a significant project, and can describe how you designed it and evaluated its reliability
Strong fundamentals in data structures, design patterns, REST API design, and relational databases
Hands-on observability experience: instrumenting applications with metrics, logs, and traces, and building dashboards and alerts
A record of learning new technologies quickly, working through ambiguity, and communicating clearly across teams
Preferred Qualifications
Shipped agentic features to production, including tool integrations, retrieval pipelines, evaluation, and guardrails
- Python, including LLM APIs or agent frameworks
- Daily use of GenAI coding tools (Claude, Copilot, Codex) to speed up development, testing, and debugging
- Schema design, query optimization, and performance tuning on PostgreSQL, Oracle, or MySQL
- Data modeling and reconciliation across multiple sources, including data-quality measurement
- Web accessibility (WCAG) and building accessible enterprise UIs
- CI/CD, Docker, Kubernetes, and cloud or virtualization platforms
- Secure software practices: security design reviews, dependency and vulnerability management, compliance
- Experience leading a project or mentoring other engineers, and contributing to inner-source or open-source projects

The Multimodal Intelligence Team is building the next generation of foundation models for Apple experiences. We are looking for a research scientist to advance the architectures, pre-training methods, and distillation techniques that make highly capable multimodal models practical across the Apple ecosystem.
Our research spans the full foundation-model lifecycle: model architecture, pre-training objectives, data mixtures, optimization, scaling, distillation, and evaluation. A defining challenge of our work is to develop models that combine broad intelligence with the memory, latency, energy, and privacy requirements of on-device deployment.
You will have the opportunity to shape new research directions, conduct ambitious experiments at scale, and translate successful ideas into foundation-model technologies that can reach Apple products. Where appropriate, this work may also lead to publications and the open sourcing of selected models, research artifacts, evaluations, or tools.
In this role, you will investigate fundamental questions about how multimodal foundation models should be designed, trained, and distilled.
You will develop and evaluate new model architectures, pre-training objectives, data strategies, optimization methods, and teacher–student learning techniques. Your work will explore how capabilities developed in large foundation models can be effectively transferred to smaller, more efficient models without treating distillation as an isolated downstream step.
A major focus of the role will be the co-development of frontier models and efficient models for Apple silicon and on-device intelligence. This includes designing architectures that distill effectively, studying how teacher and student models should be trained together, and developing distillation methods that preserve reasoning, multimodal understanding, instruction following, and other important capabilities under constrained model capacity.
Rather than treating deployment constraints as an afterthought, you will incorporate them into the research process—from early architecture experiments and pre-training through distillation and final model evaluation.
You may thrive in this role if you:
* Want to invent new foundation-model architectures rather than only adapt existing models.
* Enjoy combining scientific ambition with real compute, memory, latency, and energy constraints.
* Believe that small and efficient models can be a frontier research problem, not merely a compression exercise.
* Are comfortable working across model research, data, systems, and hardware boundaries.
* Care about translating research into private, useful, and deeply integrated intelligent experiences.
* Want your work to have both product impact and a presence in the broader research community.
Potential research directions include:
* Novel dense, recurrent, state-space, mixture-of-experts, and hybrid foundation-model architectures.
* Multimodal pre-training across language, images, video, audio, and sensor-derived representations.
* Compute-optimal model and data scaling, including data mixtures, curricula, tokenization, and training objectives.
* Architecture and algorithm co-design for memory-efficient and energy-efficient inference on Apple silicon.
* Offline and on-policy distillation using teacher-generated data, logits, representations, rationales, and other supervision signals.
Minimum Qualifications
Hands-on experience designing, implementing, and running large-scale pre-training experiments for large language models.
Experience with LLM pre-training topics such as model architecture, training objectives, data mixtures, tokenization, curricula, scaling, and optimization.
Strong proficiency with modern deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch or JAX and distributed training systems.
Experience evaluating pre-trained models across language understanding, reasoning, instruction following, or multimodal capabilities.
Strong understanding of transformer-based architectures and current approaches to efficient or scalable foundation-model training.
Master’s degree, or equivalent practical experience in machine learning, computer science, or a related technical field.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience contributing to major foundation-model pre-training efforts or leading architecture experiments that influenced a large training run.
Research contributions in model architecture, scaling laws, multimodal pre-training, optimization, efficient attention, mixture-of-experts, state-space models, or related areas.
Experience with knowledge distillation, including offline or off-policy distillation, on-policy distillation, self-distillation, sequence-level distillation, logic matching, or representation transfer.
Experience designing teacher–student training pipelines or transferring capabilities from large foundation models to smaller models.
Experience with multimodal models spanning language, vision, video, audio, or other sensor modalities.
Understanding of inference efficiency, memory hierarchy, hardware accelerators, or hardware–software co-design.
Strong publication record, influential open-source contributions, or an equivalent record of applied research impact

The Apple Services Engineering (ASE) team builds the container and virtualization runtime technology that powers Apple's next-generation compute platform. We're a fast-moving, highly skilled team of systems engineers designing and developing the virtualization-based runtimes that run Virtual Machines and Linux Containers across our data center, with privacy, security, and performance as first-class requirements.
We're starting a new team focused on one question: how do we patch the node software across our datacenter fleet faster, and more often, with minimal impact to the workloads running on it? We're looking for a domain expert to decide the approach and then build and lead the team that delivers it.
Today, updating a node's software means choosing between speed and workload impact. This team's job is to remove that tradeoff, so we can patch the fleet faster and more often with minimal impact on users. We have not chosen an approach. Live migration, snapshot and restore, kexec-based host updates, live patching, and in-place upgrade of the runtime and VMM are all options, and a different approach may fit better than any of them. We are looking for an expert to decide and guide: which approach, or combination, gets us there, what it costs in workload impact and operational risk, and how we measure the result.
You will:
* Define the fleet patching strategy: evaluate the candidate approaches (including ones we haven't listed), choose, and make the tradeoffs explicit, grounded in a model of how each one fails.
* Set the metrics that matter, such as guest-visible downtime, total migration time, network amplification, abortability, and time to patch the fleet.
* Design and drive the first implementation, building on Cloud Hypervisor and our Linux microVM runtimes on x86 and arm64.
* Hire and grow the team. Depending on your background and interests this is a technical-lead role or a people-management role, and we will decide that together.
* Work with the SRE, Compute, and security organizations on rollout, safety, and fleet operations.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, or equivalent related experience.
At least 8+ years of software design and development experience in infrastructure engineering (compute, storage and network virtualization).
Deep, demonstrated experience in one of the following, and working fluency in the other: Operating live migration, live patching, or kexec-style host updates across a production fleet, including the failures: non-convergence, aborts and rollback, and fleet-wide rollout safety. Building live migration, snapshot/restore, or device-state serialization inside a hypervisor or VMM (for example QEMU/KVM, Cloud Hypervisor, Firecracker, Xen, or Hyper-V).
Advanced programming language proficiency in C, C++, Rust, Swift or Go, with a track record of designing and developing high performance, secured, scalable and reliable systems.
Track record of owning technical design end-to-end, from design docs and architecture tradeoffs through implementation and review.
Experience setting technical direction for a group of engineers, with or without formal management responsibility.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with Linux kernel and system programming (KVM, userfaultfd, VFIO, kexec, kernel live patching).
Understanding of dirty-page tracking, memory and device state handling, and time and CPU-model compatibility across hosts.
Experience with live migration of devices that carry hardware state (VFIO, vDPA, SR-IOV).
Experience designing benchmarks and load tests to characterize downtime and performance impact during an upgrade.
Experience contributing to or maintaining open source virtualization projects (Cloud Hypervisor, rust-vmm, QEMU, KVM).
Experience with Kubernetes node lifecycle, draining, and fleet rollout orchestration.
Experience building a new team from zero, including hiring.

The ACAI Training & Inference Platform team is seeking a Senior / Staff Software Engineer with strong distributed systems expertise and deep experience in AI training and inference. As part of Apple Cloud AI (ACAI) within Apple’s Data Platform (ADP), you will design and build core capabilities for large-scale model training, post-training, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and high-performance inference.
You will develop scalable AI execution frameworks, developer-facing APIs, and runtime optimizations that make it easier to train, adapt, and serve advanced models efficiently across Apple’s AI ecosystem. You will partner closely with AI researchers and engineers to translate evolving model architectures and workload requirements into reliable, high-performance training and inference solutions. This role is ideal for an engineer who combines deep distributed-systems expertise with hands-on knowledge of modern LLM training, post-training, and inference optimization.
ADP brings together the Apple Cloud Data Platform (ACDP), Apple Cloud AI (ACAI), and Apple Governance Platform (AGP) to provide foundational capabilities for data, analytics, AI, and governance at Apple scale. Within ACAI, the Training & Inference Platform team enables scalable model development and production inference across Apple’s AI ecosystem.
As a Senior / Staff Software Engineer, you will build capabilities spanning the model lifecycle, from distributed training and post-training to optimized inference and serving.
On the training side, you will develop frameworks and APIs for fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and post-training workflows, enabling AI teams to efficiently adapt foundation models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), preference optimization, and reinforcement learning from feedback or verifiable rewards. You will simplify the execution of complex training pipelines, improve experimentation and iteration speed, and enable reusable, production-ready training workflows.
On the inference side, you will drive deep runtime and LLM-serving optimizations to improve throughput, reduce latency, and lower the cost of serving both real time and batch inference workloads. You will optimize execution across heterogeneous hardware and model architectures, leveraging techniques such as continuous batching, KV-cache optimization, quantization, speculative decoding, disaggregated prefill and decode, and efficient distributed inference.
Across both areas, you will improve the performance, scalability, reliability, and developer experience of AI training and inference workloads. You will work closely with AI practitioners to identify bottlenecks across model execution, scheduling, communication, and resource utilization, translating these insights into end-to-end improvements in model development and serving efficiency.

Apple has changed how people live, connect, and work, and the Calendar team wants to rethink what a calendar can do for the people using it. A calendar knows when someone is busy. It knows very little about which of those commitments matter, which ones could move, or when would be a good time for something new. We're looking for an engineer to help answer those questions, on device and privately, for billions of people. The right person has strong machine learning foundations and is just as comfortable writing the software that ships a model as building the model itself. You'll help take ideas from a single sentence to a shipped feature, and you'll bring the evaluation that tells us whether it works.
In this role you'll drive the modeling and evaluation behind intelligence features in Calendar, from the first framing through launch, as part of a very collaborative team. A request will often start as one line, and you'll work with the team to turn it into a problem we can solve: what signal exists, what a good answer looks like, which approach fits, and how we'll know it's right. You'll design the evaluation before you build the model. That means the metrics, the eval sets, the baselines a model has to beat, and human review for the places where a metric can't tell you enough.
You won't always have good data, so part of the job is finding it and getting something useful out of it when there isn't much. You'll need to get real statistical strength out of priors, shared structure, and self-supervision. You'll also work with a range of large language models, on device and on server, deciding where a model call earns its cost, where a smaller model trained on a larger model's judgments does better, and where a well-tuned heuristic beats both.
You'll join a small team of senior systems engineers who ship this work across Apple's platforms, several of them with deep backgrounds in ML data engineering. There's no hard line between roles, so you'll write production code alongside them in whatever part of the stack the problem needs. Calendar also builds on signals and models from other ML teams across Apple, and a lot of this role is working with them: building on what they have, agreeing on shared interfaces, and recognizing when we need our own. You'll work closely with design and product as well. We need someone who writes clearly, can explain a model's tradeoffs to engineers who aren't ML specialists, and is comfortable driving a problem forward before the path is defined.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, EE, Applied Mathematics, or related field with 2+ years experience in developing ML / AI driven software.
Proficiency in one or more of the following programming languages: Python, Swift, Objective-C, or C++
Experience developing software prototypes and features driven by Large Language Models and designing tool and function-calling interfaces, constructing context, and validating model output
Fluency with agentic coding tools such as Claude Code, with good judgment about where to apply them and how to verify what they produce.
Experience driving an ambiguous problem with cross-functional partners, including other ML teams, from a loose idea through launch, and getting alignment on shared interfaces along the way.
Exceptional problem-solving skills, and the ability to drive alignment across teams on shared API surfaces
Preferred Qualifications
Experience designing and developing systems that are efficient in resource constrained environments — latency, memory, and power budgets on device
Solid foundation in machine learning, probability, and statistics, with hands-on experience training and evaluating models in a framework such as PyTorch or JAX
A track record of designing the evaluation for what you ship: metrics, held-out sets, baselines, and noticing when a metric has stopped measuring what you care about
Proven ability to excel in a fast-paced development team

As part of our Silicon Technologies group, you’ll help design and manufacture our next-generation, high-performance, power-efficient processor, system-on-chip (SoC). Together, you and your team will enable our customers to do all the things they love with their devices. We promote innovation and new technology. The people who work here have reinvented and defined entire industries with the Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, Apple Watch, AirPods, HomePod and a multitude of groundbreaking Accessories. The same passion for innovation that goes into our products also applies to our practices — strengthening our dedication to leave the world better than we found it. You should join us to help deliver the next amazing Apple product. We are seeking a multifaceted engineer to develop system level test programs for debug, characterization, qualification, and production of SoC devices. Are you ready for a challenge?!
- Perform measurements that directly impact SoC power & performance for various next generation products.
- Work on groundbreaking technologies & new designs and collaborate with multiple multi-functional teams including design, validation, test, manufacturing, system test & software to identify issues and implement corrective actions.
- Work closely with ATE and software teams to identify & develop case tests, benchmarks to be used in production testing, and characterization.
- Characterize multiple test setups, correlate to ATE and optimize production screening guardband for each system individually.
- Define characterization plans, perform statistical data analysis and drive correlation & data reviews across multiple cross-functional teams and sign off on all silicon characterization activities.
- Multi-task and manage multiple programs at different stages
- Central point of contact for multiple teams with direct impact on product.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree + 10 Years of Experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with system level characterization using functional / virus like worst case use cases & correlating to ATE.
Understanding of PDN impact on Vmin, ATE test content, system level test programs/ functional content and test hardware.
Experience working with and driving cross functional teams
Statistical data analysis tools to perform high volume characterization & production data analysis.
Experience in scripting (Python, JMP, PERL etc.) is a plus.
